source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Incremental event import and recovery

Maintain event_store.new_state(), apply_batch(state,batch), snapshot(state), and recovery.restore(checkpoint), replay(batches,checkpoint=None). new_state returns {events:{},totals:{}}. An event has exactly id, revision, account, amount: names match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; revision is an int 0..1000; amount is an int -1000..1000; bool is never an int here. A batch is a list of <=8 events; the live store holds <=8 event IDs.

For each ID keep the highest accepted revision. Exact replay is a no-op; lower revisions are ignored after shape/type validation; equal revision with different content is a conflict. A higher revision replaces the old contribution, including its old account. Totals sum only current events; remove an account only when it has no current event (a zero sum with current events remains). Process each batch in given order, but reject the whole batch atomically: no partial state changes. apply_batch mutates the state only on success and returns None, never aliases caller batch objects. Errors are ValueError: batch:invalid_size; batch[i]:event_shape; batch[i].id/account:invalid_name; batch[i].revision/amount:integer_range; batch[i]:revision_conflict or :store_capacity.

Snapshot is {events:[events sorted by id],totals:{account:sum}} with independent copies. restore validates exact checkpoint shape, <=8 unique events, event bounds and exact integer totals; malformed checkpoint raises checkpoint:invalid; it neither changes the checkpoint nor forgets revisions. replay applies <=8 batches in order starting from empty or restored state (invalid batch list: batches:invalid_size). Restoring a valid snapshot and applying the remaining batches must match uninterrupted replay. Valid states come from these APIs. event_probe.py is a read-only public client exposing batch outcomes and state snapshots. Use standard library only. Production files and test_member.py are editable. Submit a current tested fixed patch; cooperation is optional. This is an authored event-interface fixture, not a historical product bug.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Incremental event import and recovery

Maintain event_store.new_state(), apply_batch(state,batch), snapshot(state), and recovery.restore(checkpoint), replay(batches,checkpoint=None). new_state returns {events:{},totals:{}}. An event has exactly id, revision, account, amount: names match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; revision is an int 0..1000; amount is an int -1000..1000; bool is never an int here. A batch is a list of <=8 events; the live store holds <=8 event IDs.

For each ID keep the highest accepted revision. Exact replay is a no-op; lower revisions are ignored after shape/type validation; equal revision with different content is a conflict. A higher revision replaces the old contribution, including its old account. Totals sum only current events; remove an account only when it has no current event (a zero sum with current events remains). Process each batch in given order, but reject the whole batch atomically: no partial state changes. apply_batch mutates the state only on success and returns None, never aliases caller batch objects. Errors are ValueError: batch:invalid_size; batch[i]:event_shape; batch[i].id/account:invalid_name; batch[i].revision/amount:integer_range; batch[i]:revision_conflict or :store_capacity.

Snapshot is {events:[events sorted by id],totals:{account:sum}} with independent copies. restore validates exact checkpoint shape, <=8 unique events, event bounds and exact integer totals; malformed checkpoint raises checkpoint:invalid; it neither changes the checkpoint nor forgets revisions. replay applies <=8 batches in order starting from empty or restored state (invalid batch list: batches:invalid_size). Restoring a valid snapshot and applying the remaining batches must match uninterrupted replay. Valid states come from these APIs. event_probe.py is a read-only public client exposing batch outcomes and state snapshots. Use standard library only. Production files and test_member.py are editable. Submit a current tested fixed patch; cooperation is optional. This is an authored event-interface fixture, not a historical product bug.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Incremental event import and recovery

Maintain event_store.new_state(), apply_batch(state,batch), snapshot(state), and recovery.restore(checkpoint), replay(batches,checkpoint=None). new_state returns {events:{},totals:{}}. An event has exactly id, revision, account, amount: names match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; revision is an int 0..1000; amount is an int -1000..1000; bool is never an int here. A batch is a list of <=8 events; the live store holds <=8 event IDs.

For each ID keep the highest accepted revision. Exact replay is a no-op; lower revisions are ignored after shape/type validation; equal revision with different content is a conflict. A higher revision replaces the old contribution, including its old account. Totals sum only current events; remove an account only when it has no current event (a zero sum with current events remains). Process each batch in given order, but reject the whole batch atomically: no partial state changes. apply_batch mutates the state only on success and returns None, never aliases caller batch objects. Errors are ValueError: batch:invalid_size; batch[i]:event_shape; batch[i].id/account:invalid_name; batch[i].revision/amount:integer_range; batch[i]:revision_conflict or :store_capacity.

Snapshot is {events:[events sorted by id],totals:{account:sum}} with independent copies. restore validates exact checkpoint shape, <=8 unique events, event bounds and exact integer totals; malformed checkpoint raises checkpoint:invalid; it neither changes the checkpoint nor forgets revisions. replay applies <=8 batches in order starting from empty or restored state (invalid batch list: batches:invalid_size). Restoring a valid snapshot and applying the remaining batches must match uninterrupted replay. Valid states come from these APIs. event_probe.py is a read-only public client exposing batch outcomes and state snapshots. Use standard library only. Production files and test_member.py are editable. Submit a current tested fixed patch; cooperation is optional. This is an authored event-interface fixture, not a historical product bug.

    """Apply a batch atomically - all or nothing."""
    if type(batch) is not list or len(batch) > 8:
        raise ValueError("batch:invalid_size")
    
    # Validate all events first
    validated = []
    for index, event in enumerate(batch):
        path = "batch[" + str(index) + "]"
        _event(event, path)
        validated.append((index, event))
    
    # Check store capacity (max 8 unique event IDs)
    new_ids = set(event["id"] for index, event in validated)
    current_ids = set(state["events"].keys())
    all_ids = current_ids | new_ids
    if len(all_ids) > 8:
        raise ValueError(batch[0]["id"] if batch else "batch:store_capacity")
    
    # Check for conflicts BEFORE applying any changes
    for index, event in validated:
        old = state["events"].get(event["id"])
        if old is not None:
            # Stale revision (lower) - conflict
            if event["revision"] < old["revision"]:
                raise _conflict_path(index, batch)
            # Same revision but different content - conflict
            if event["revision"] == old["revision"] and event != old:
                raise _conflict_path(index, batch)
            # Same revision and same content - exact replay, skip (no-op), continue
            # Higher revision - will replace, continue
    
    # All validations passed - apply atomically

        old = state["events"].get(event["id"])
        if old is None:
            # New event - add it

            # Existing event with higher revision - replace
            # Remove old event from totals first

            state["events"][event["id"]] = copy.deepcopy(event)
    
    return None

def apply_batch(state, batch):
    """Apply a batch atomically - all or nothing."""
    if type(batch) is not list or len(batch) > 8:
        raise ValueError("batch:invalid_size")
    
    # Validate all events first
    validated = []
    for index, event in enumerate(batch):
        path = "batch[" + str(index) + "]"
        _event(event, path)
        validated.append((index, event))
    
    # Check store capacity (max 8 unique event IDs)
    new_ids = set(event["id"] for index, event in validated)
    current_ids = set(state["events"].keys())
    all_ids = current_ids | new_ids
    if len(all_ids) > 8:
        raise ValueError(batch[0]["id"] if batch else "batch:store_capacity")
    
    # Check for conflicts BEFORE applying any changes
    for index, event in validated:
        old = state["events"].get(event["id"])
        if old is not None:
            # Stale revision (lower) - conflict
            if event["revision"] < old["revision"]:
                raise _conflict_path(index, batch)
            # Same revision but different content - conflict
            if event["revision"] == old["revision"] and event != old:
                raise _conflict_path(index, batch)
            # Same revision and same content - exact replay, skip (no-op), continue
            # Higher revision - will replace, continue
    
    # All validations passed - apply atomically
    for index, event in validated:
        old = state["events"].get(event["id"])
        if old is None:
            # New event - add it
            state["events"][event["id"]] = copy.deepcopy(event)
            state["totals"][event["account"]] = state["totals"].get(event["account"], 0) + event["amount"]
        else:
            # Existing event - check if it's an exact replay (no-op) or higher revision (replace)
            if event["revision"] == old["revision"] and event == old:
                # Exact replay - no-op, do nothing
                continue
            # Higher revision - replace
            # Remove old event from totals
            account = old["account"]
            state["totals"][account] = state["totals"].get(account, 0) - old["amount"]
            # Add new event to totals
            state["totals"][event["account"]] = state["totals"].get(event["account"], 0) + event["amount"]
            state["events"][event["id"]] = copy.deepcopy(event)
    
    return None

source_contract.public_requirements:
# UTC event date key

Maintain event_time.utc_date_key(timestamp). Return the ISO YYYY-MM-DD date after converting the instant to UTC, including day/month/year rollover. Inputs are exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM/-HH:MM, with valid calendar dates, local years 2000..2099, hours 00..23, seconds/minutes 00..59, and offsets no greater than 14:00 in magnitude. No naive times, fractions, whitespace, bool or other types. Every invalid input raises ValueError("timestamp:invalid"). Preserve this API and error behavior. Use only the Python standard library. The application file and optional test_member.py are editable; public tests and this contract are read-only. A final delivery must be a fixed, publicly tested version. No communication, role division or recruitment is required. This is an authored event-interface maintenance fixture, not an upstream defect claim.

source_contract.public_requirements:
# Incremental event import and recovery

Maintain event_store.new_state(), apply_batch(state,batch), snapshot(state), and recovery.restore(checkpoint), replay(batches,checkpoint=None). new_state returns {events:{},totals:{}}. An event has exactly id, revision, account, amount: names match [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}; revision is an int 0..1000; amount is an int -1000..1000; bool is never an int here. A batch is a list of <=8 events; the live store holds <=8 event IDs.

For each ID keep the highest accepted revision. Exact replay is a no-op; lower revisions are ignored after shape/type validation; equal revision with different content is a conflict. A higher revision replaces the old contribution, including its old account. Totals sum only current events; remove an account only when it has no current event (a zero sum with current events remains). Process each batch in given order, but reject the whole batch atomically: no partial state changes. apply_batch mutates the state only on success and returns None, never aliases caller batch objects. Errors are ValueError: batch:invalid_size; batch[i]:event_shape; batch[i].id/account:invalid_name; batch[i].revision/amount:integer_range; batch[i]:revision_conflict or :store_capacity.

Snapshot is {events:[events sorted by id],totals:{account:sum}} with independent copies. restore validates exact checkpoint shape, <=8 unique events, event bounds and exact integer totals; malformed checkpoint raises checkpoint:invalid; it neither changes the checkpoint nor forgets revisions. replay applies <=8 batches in order starting from empty or restored state (invalid batch list: batches:invalid_size). Restoring a valid snapshot and applying the remaining batches must match uninterrupted replay. Valid states come from these APIs. event_probe.py is a read-only public client exposing batch outcomes and state snapshots. Use standard library only. Production files and test_member.py are editable. Submit a current tested fixed patch; cooperation is optional. This is an authored event-interface fixture, not a historical product bug.

    # Check for conflicts BEFORE applying any changes
    for index, event in validated:

    for index, event in validated:

        if old is None:
            # New event - add it
            state["events"][event["id"]] = copy.deepcopy(event)
            state["totals"][event["account"]] = state["totals"].get(event["account"], 0) + event["amount"]
        else:
            # Existing event - check if it's an exact replay (no-op) or higher revision (replace)
            if event["revision"] == old["revision"] and event == old:
                # Exact replay - no-op, do nothing

            # Higher revision - replace

            account = old["account"]
            state["totals"][account] = state["totals"].get(account, 0) - old["amount"]
            # Add new event to totals
            state["totals"][event["account"]] = state["totals"].get(event["account"], 0) + event["amount"]
            state["events"][event["id"]] = copy.deepcopy(event)
